l2_natural: Could I have some water, please?
l2_simple: Can I have water, please?
notes_l1: Bir şey isterken 'Can I have...' kalıbı en doğal yoldur.

l2_natural: I'm Berat. Nice to meet you.
l2_simple: My name is Berat. Nice to meet you.
notes_l1: 'I'm' (I am) demek daha doğal ve yaygındır.

l2_natural: Could you please speak more slowly?
l2_simple: Can you speak slowly, please?
notes_l1: Derslerde öğretmenden ricada bulunurken 'Can you... please?' kalıbı çok kullanışlıdır.

l2_natural: Where is the bathroom?
l2_simple: Where is the bathroom?
notes_l1: Restroom da diyebilirsiniz, özellikle restoranlarda veya iş yerlerinde daha yaygındır.

l2_natural: I love you, good night.
l2_simple: I love you, good night.
notes_l1: Sevdiklerine söylerken kullanılır.

l2_natural: I was very busy today, so I'll be home late.
l2_simple: I was very busy today. I will come home late.
notes_l1: 'I will' yerine konuşurken 'I'll' demek çok yaygındır.

l2_natural: I have a question.
l2_simple: I have a question.
notes_l1: Dersi bölmeden sormak isterseniz 'Excuse me, I have a question' diyebilirsiniz.

l2_natural: I'm sorry, I forgot to do my homework.
l2_simple: I forgot to do my homework.
notes_l1: Öğretmeninize karşı 'I'm sorry' (üzgünüm/kusura bakmayın) eklemek çok nazik bir davranıştır.

l2_natural: What shall we have for dinner?
l2_simple: What do you want to eat for dinner?
notes_l1: 'Shall we' öneri sunarken kullanılır ama günlük dilde 'What do you want to...' daha yaygındır.

l2_natural: Can I pay by card?
l2_simple: Can I pay by card?
notes_l1: İngilizcede kartla ödeme yaparken 'pay by card' veya 'pay with card' diyebilirsin.

l2_natural: I missed the bus, so I'm late.
l2_simple: I missed the bus, so I am late.
notes_l1: So, iki cümleyi 'bu yüzden' anlamında bağlar.

l2_natural: I visited my family this weekend.
l2_simple: I visited my family this weekend.
notes_l1: 'Visit' fiili Türkçedeki ziyaret etmek ile aynıdır.

l2_natural: My favorite character in this show is his brother.
l2_simple: My favorite character in this show is his brother.
notes_l1: Dizi için 'show' veya 'series' kelimelerini kullanabilirsin.

l2_natural: Could you cook today?
l2_simple: Can you cook today?
notes_l1: Birinden bir şey rica ederken 'Can you...?' kullanmak en kolay ve yaygın yoldur.

l2_natural: I have a headache. Is the pharmacy open?
l2_simple: I have a headache. Is the pharmacy open?
notes_l1: İngilizcede hastalıklar için 'have' kullanılır: I have a headache, I have a cold.

l2_natural: What does this word mean?
l2_simple: What does this word mean?
notes_l1: Öğretmenine veya arkadaşına bir kelimeyi sorarken her zaman bu kalıbı kullanabilirsin.

l2_natural: Could we have the bill, please?
l2_simple: Can I have the bill, please?
notes_l1: ABD'de 'check', İngiltere ve diğer ülkelerde 'bill' kullanılır.

l2_natural: My favorite season is autumn because the weather is cool.
l2_simple: My favorite season is autumn because the weather is cool.
notes_l1: Autumn yerine 'fall' kelimesini de kullanabilirsiniz (özellikle Amerika'da yaygındır).

l2_natural: Is it going to rain tomorrow?
l2_simple: Will it rain tomorrow?
notes_l1: İki kullanım da doğrudur, 'Will it rain' başlangıç seviyesi için daha kolaydır.

l2_natural: I'm bored. Let's go out!
l2_simple: I'm bored. Let's go out!
notes_l1: Bir öneride bulunurken 'Let's + fiil' yapısını kullanırız.

l2_natural: I'd like to make a reservation for two for tonight, please.
l2_simple: I want to make a reservation for two people tonight.
notes_l1: İki kişi için derken 'two people' veya sadece 'two' denir.

l2_natural: I'm sorry, I can't hear you.
l2_simple: I can't hear you.
notes_l1: Online derslerde 'I can't hear you' en yaygın ve doğru ifadedir.

l2_natural: Sorry, my internet cut out. I didn't catch the last part.
l2_simple: Sorry, my internet cut out. I didn't hear the last part.
notes_l1: İnternet bağlantısı kesildiğinde veya koptuğunda 'cut out' en yaygın kullanılan ifadedir.

l2_natural: Do you have this shirt in a larger size?
l2_simple: Do you have this in a bigger size?
notes_l1: Mağazada kıyafet sorarken 'Do you have this in...?' kalıbını kullanabilirsin.

l2_natural: I'd like to cancel my reservation, please.
l2_simple: I want to cancel my reservation.
notes_l1: İsteklerinizi daha kibar ifade etmek için 'I'd like to' kalıbı 'I want'tan daha uygundur.

l2_natural: What's the difference between these two sentences?
l2_simple: What's the difference between these two sentences?
notes_l1: Bir şeylerin arasındaki farkı sorarken 'difference between X and Y' yapısını kullanırız.

l2_natural: Our neighbor's dog was barking all night.
l2_simple: Our neighbor's dog barked all night.
notes_l1: 'Bark' köpek havlaması demektir.

l2_natural: What I like most about my job is working with people.
l2_simple: I like working with people most in my job.
notes_l1: Bir şeyi en çok sevdiğinizi belirtmek için 'What I like most is...' yapısı çok yaygındır.

l2_natural: The end of the movie really surprised me.
l2_simple: The end of the movie surprised me a lot.
notes_l1: 'The end of the movie' yerine 'the ending' de diyebilirsin.

l2_natural: The meeting has been moved to 3 o'clock.
l2_simple: The meeting is at 3 o'clock now.
notes_l1: Bir şeyin saatinin değiştirildiğini belirtmek için 'moved' kelimesi çok yaygındır.

l2_natural: Let's not make any plans this weekend; let's just relax.
l2_simple: Let's not plan anything this weekend, let's just rest.
notes_l1: Bir teklifte bulunurken 'Let's' kullanmak çok yaygındır.

l2_natural: My package still hasn't arrived. Could you help me track it?
l2_simple: My package is not here yet. Can you tell me where it is?
notes_l1: Bir paketin nerede olduğunu sormak için 'track' (takip etmek) fiilini de kullanabilirsin.

l2_natural: Is my pronunciation correct?
l2_simple: Is my pronunciation correct?
notes_l1: 'Pronunciation' kelimesini telaffuz ederken dikkatli ol; 'pro-nun-si-ey-şın' gibi okunur.

l2_natural: Could you do me a favor?
l2_simple: Can you do me a favor?
notes_l1: 'Could' ile sormak her zaman daha kibardır.

l2_natural: I'm just kidding.
l2_simple: I am joking.
notes_l1: İnsanlar 'I'm kidding' ifadesini de çok sık kullanır.

l2_natural: I'm thinking of working abroad next year.
l2_simple: I am planning to work abroad next year.
notes_l1: 'Abroad' yurt dışı demektir. Bir planından bahsederken 'I'm planning to' (planlıyorum) demek daha kesin bir ifade katar.

l2_natural: I'd like to return this, please. I have the receipt with me.
l2_simple: Can I return this, please? Here is the receipt.
notes_l1: 'Receipt' fiş demektir, telaffuzu 'risit' şeklindedir, 'p' okunmaz.

l2_natural: Could you please elaborate on that a bit? It hasn't quite clicked for me yet.
l2_simple: Could you explain that more, please? I don't fully understand it yet.
notes_l1: To 'elaborate' means to explain more details. Saying 'it hasn't clicked' is a common way to say you don't fully understand or grasp something yet.

l2_natural: I need to renew my lease.
l2_simple: I need to renew my rental agreement.
notes_l1: In the US, people usually say 'lease' for housing contracts. 'Rental agreement' is also correct but slightly more formal.

l2_natural: I wish we didn't leave everything until the last minute.
l2_simple: I wish we didn't leave everything to the last minute.
notes_l1: Use 'I wish we didn't' for something happening now that you want to be different.

l2_natural: I think working from home has both its pros and cons.
l2_simple: I think working from home has some good and bad points.
notes_l1: 'Pros and cons' is a common idiom meaning advantages and disadvantages.

l2_natural: This episode was a bit dull compared to the others.
l2_simple: This episode was a bit boring compared to the other ones.
notes_l1: When talking about shows or movies, using 'dull' or 'slow' is often more natural than 'boring'.
